transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-07-15 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (Aurora Head of Security), Derek Wong (Platform Eng), Leila Hassan (PM)

Summary:
Weekly POC check-in focused on security/compliance items for the pilot: SSO/SAML testing, audit logs and retention, SOC2 scoping, KMS/encryption, and RBAC. Reviewed recent test results, surfaced gaps, agreed next steps and owners.

Topics:
- SSO/SAML integration status and test failures
- Audit logs: events, retention, export and access controls
- Data retention & data residency questions during pilot
- SOC2/attestation timeline and evidence needs
- Encryption/KMS and key management during POC
- Roles, RBAC, and access provisioning for audit reviewers

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep this to 45. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Marta Ruiz: Marta here.
[00:08] Derek Wong: Derek on the line.
[00:10] Leila Hassan: Leila here.
[00:12] Priya Nair: Priya from Redwood. Alex?
[00:15] Alex Chen: Cool, thanks. Agenda is mostly security follow-ups from last week, SSO and audit logs, SOC2 scoping. Priya, do you want to start with SSO?
[02:05] Priya Nair: Sure. So we re-ran the SAML flow against Aurora's IdP test tenant. We got the same failure you saw last week, it's around the assertion consumer URL mismatch and a signed-assertion flag, basically the SAML response includes an embedded audience value that our metadata parser flagged. In the logs it shows 401-ish behavior, but because of the IdP the error message is a bit unhelpful.
[03:00] Derek Wong: Yeah we saw that. Our IdP team said the ACS was set to the long URL and your metadata had the short URL, small mismatch. We can change that but we wanted to confirm there's no expected behavior on Redwood side blocking the signature algorithm.
[03:22] Priya Nair: Good question. We support SHA-256 signatures and the authn context we accept is the default OIDC-ish SAML profile, but there is a config flag in the Redwood console to accept multiple ACS aliases. I can send the exact flag name. Also note in our hosted flow the redirect URI normalization is applied which might alter the incoming ACS path, so best practice is to use the exact metadata we provide.
[04:05] Alex Chen: Action: Alex will send the SSO metadata and a short checklist.
[06:10] Marta Ruiz: From a security perspective we need to test with our production IdP eventually. For the POC we want assurance the SSO integration can be done without exchanging long-lived credentials, ideally just SAML metadata and SCIM for provisioning.
[07:30] Priya Nair: We support SCIM for user provisioning; you'll need to generate a SCIM bearer token via the console and we support role mapping. Note: the SCIM endpoints are behind RBAC so only tokened service accounts see user resources.
[09:00] Leila Hassan: On provisioning, can we map groups to roles so auditors only see read-only views?
[09:15] Priya Nair: Yes, group mapping to RBAC is supported. We have built-in roles and also custom role templates. The only caveat during POC is the console UI for fine-grained role editing is gated behind dedicated accounts, but we can apply mappings via API quickly.
[11:45] Derek Wong: Switching to audit logs. We need to know what events you retain, how long, and how logs are exported. Also who can access logs and are they immutable?
[12:10] Priya Nair: Current POC default is 90 day retention for detailed request logs and 365 for aggregated metrics. We offer an export to your S3 bucket or syslog endpoint; exports are batched hourly by default. Logs are append-only and digested with an HMAC so tamper-evidence is available; we also store write-audit trails for changes to retention settings.
[12:48] Marta Ruiz: HMAC tamper evidence is good, can we get the keys used for that? Is that customer-controlled?
[13:05] Priya Nair: Good point. For hosted customers the HMAC keys are managed by Redwood KMS. For Dedicated or Private installs we can integrate with your KMS/HSM; for the POC we can do a demonstration of key rotation.
[14:30] Alex Chen: Note: Aurora flagged regulatory requirements around payments data. Are there any concerns about PII in logs?
[14:50] Derek Wong: Yes logs may contain masked card identifiers and truncated PAN fragments; we want to ensure no full PANs are ever written and a redaction policy exists.
[15:10] Priya Nair: Our ingestion pipeline applies redaction rules by default - credit card numbers are redacted to last 4 only, and full payloads with sensitive fields are excluded unless you opt-in. We can show the redaction rules in the demo.
[17:00] Leila Hassan: Can retention be set per-log-type? For example, we want request debug logs for 30 days but auth events for 2 years.
[17:20] Priya Nair: Yes, retention is per-log-class. During POC we can configure those policies; in the hosted plan we had some UI limits but via API and config you can set per-class retention.
[19:45] Marta Ruiz: SOC2 question - does Redwood have a current Type II report and can you share scoping docs? Which systems are included?
[20:05] Alex Chen: Redwood is SOC2 Type II certified for the hosted platform as of 2024-10; we have a summary and a long-form assertion. For the POC we'll share the SOC2 summary and a list of controls mapped to our services. For Private installs, Redwood provides attestation support but the private environment may require additional evidence.
[21:40] Marta Ruiz: Ok we'd like to see the mapping doc and understand if audit evidence (log exports, config change history) is included.
[22:00] Priya Nair: We'll include the evidence mapping. Note: some evidence items are self-hosted for dedicated/private runs, e.g., KMS control. We'll flag those.
[24:10] Derek Wong: On encryption at rest and keys: during POC are keys customer-managed or Redwood-managed? We need to demonstrate key separation for audit.
[24:35] Priya Nair: For the hosted POC keys are Redwood-managed but we can offer bring-your-own-key (BYOK) for Dedicated/PV pilots. For the POC we can set up a test KMS integration so you can see key rotations and key usage logs.
[26:55] Marta Ruiz: Any concerns about data residency for EU transactions? Aurora processes EU cards and we need to ensure logs and tokenized data stay in EU region.
[27:15] Alex Chen: Right now the POC is in us-east but we can deploy a regionally isolated pilot in eu-west-1; that would require a dedicated instance and additional config. It's feasible but will add setup time.
[28:40] Leila Hassan: Timeline question: If we want a EU pilot, how long to stand up?
[29:00] Priya Nair: For a dedicated EU pilot it's about 2-3 weeks for infra provisioning plus config and SSO testing. For hosted region pinning it's faster but less isolated.
[31:10] Derek Wong: About access controls: we need read-only access for auditors and a way to revoke access quickly. How's session management handled?
[31:30] Priya Nair: Sessions are tied to SSO session tokens and TTLs are configurable on the IdP side. For console API keys we support short-lived tokens and rotation. We also have an admin action to force global session revocation.
[33:05] Marta Ruiz: For auditability we need immutable change logs for RBAC changes with actor and timestamp. Is that in place?
[33:20] Priya Nair: Yes change history is recorded and included in the audit log bucket. We retain those events per your retention policy and exports include the actor metadata.
[35:40] Alex Chen: Quick demo note - Priya will run a short export of an audit log and show redaction and export to S3 after the call. Priya?
[36:00] Priya Nair: Yes I'll run the export and share screenshots and the S3 manifest. Expect that in the follow-up doc.
[37:45] Leila Hassan: One more on legal/procurement: Aurora's procurement asked if there's a data processing addendum and standard SCCs for EU transfers.
[38:05] Alex Chen: We have a DPA template and standard contractual clauses; legal can share them once we reach procurement phase. I'll include a pointer in the follow-up.
[39:20] Marta Ruiz: Any blockers from Redwood side for us to start onboarding non-prod data into the POC? We want to ingest tokenized transactions and run a few end-to-end queries.
[39:35] Priya Nair: No blockers. We recommend a sanitized tokenized dataset for the first ingest. We'll provide a sample ingestion plan and data schema mapping. Also we can enable additional masking rules on ingestion if you want.
[41:10] Derek Wong: Performance quick check - can you confirm token-level latency when audit logging is enabled? We saw a slight bump last week.
[41:30] Priya Nair: That was expected due to synchronous log writes in that config. We've got a tuning option where logs are buffered and acked asynchronously; that brings latency back down but increases time-to-availability in the log store. We'll run the PV test and post results.
[42:55] Alex Chen: Great. Let's recap next steps and owners.
[43:10] Marta Ruiz: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[44:00] Alex Chen: End of call, will follow up with SSO metadata, SOC2 mapping, and the audit export.
